headline: Pantry Renovation: How to Avoid Common Mistakes
articleBody: Pantry renovations can dramatically improve your kitchen's organization, but it's easy to fall into some common traps if you're not careful. Avoiding these missteps will ensure your new pantry is truly a game-changer. One frequent mistake is creating shelves that are too deep. While you might think deeper is better, shelves much beyond 18 inches can make items get lost in the back, leading to forgotten food and wasted space. Another common oversight is neglecting door swing and aisle clearance. You need to be able to open your pantry door fully and comfortably maneuver inside or in front of a reach-in. Don't forget about placing everyday items at an easily reachable height – between 15 and 48 inches off the floor is ideal; putting frequently used goods too high or too low can be frustrating. Many people also treat tall pantry cabinets as a catch-all, when a thoughtful design with varied storage types for different items is much more effective. Finally, always think about appliance locations and electrical capacity if you plan to keep small appliances in your pantry.
